subject: MSA redline: DPA scope, SCCs mapping & subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@eurythmicshealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@eurythmicshealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + SCCs mapping questions

Neha —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached is our redline of Redwood's DPA (Eurythmics_DPA_redline_v1.docx) and a short SCCs mapping workbook. Two quick asks up front:

1) We want SCCs to be invoked via annex (not a link reference) and require mapping to subprocessor locations for EU export control review.
2) The Order Form still references an earlier data routing paragraph (Section 4) — we redlined to require prior notice + 30-day approval for any new subprocessor outside the EU/EEA.

Could you confirm Redwood's position on:
- Whether you can accept SCCs by annex and commit to subsprocessor notification windows, and
- Who on your side will own the transfer-impact addendum (TIA) evidence list?

We are on a tight procurement timeline (closing target: 30 May). If it's helpful, happy to jump on a 30-minute alignment call early next week.

Thanks,

Sarah Whitman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Eurythmics Health
[sarah.whitman@eurythmicshealth.com]

Attachments: Eurythmics_DPA_redline_v1.docx; SCCs_mapping_table.xlsx

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@eurythmicshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -07:00

Sarah —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Quick read-through and next steps from our side:

- We can accept SCCs incorporated as an annex (noted). We need to confirm operational controls for the subprocessor notification timeline — Ben will own the operational confirmation.
- For the TIA evidence list, Laura (Legal Ops) will coordinate what we can provide by category (e.g., export controls, subprocessor inventory, KMS residency).

Proposed short plan:
1) Ben to confirm subprocessor notification SLA and whether the 30-day approval window is feasible or we propose 14-day notice + escalation for high-risk locations.
2) Laura to assemble a preliminary evidence manifest aligned to your SCCs_mapping_table (ETA Tue 22 Apr).
3) If that aligns, we can bake the annex into the final MSA and provide a clean Order Form (we've tracked changes in OrderForm_v3-track-changes.docx).

Would you be available Mon 21 Apr 09:00–10:00 PT / Tue 22 Apr 14:00–15:00 PT for a 30-minute sync?

Best,

Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCCs mapping questions

Neha / team —

Quick operational take after reviewing Sarah's redlines and our current subprocessor registry:

Highlights / suggested language edits:
- Subprocessor notice: Eurythmics asks for 30-day approval for any non-EU subprocessor. Operationally, we can commit to 14-day prior notice + 30-day remediate/mitigate period for high-risk locations. Proposed wording: "Redwood will provide prior written notice of any subprocessor engagement; where the subprocessor is located outside the EU/EEA and presents material export-risk, Customer may request a 30-day review period."
- SCCs Annex: agree to annex in full. We should add an explicit cross-reference in the Order Form (Order Form §9) so downstream systems (provisioning and billing) know the applicable annex version.
- TIA evidence: KMS residency and key control evidence are the two items that typically trigger longer legal review. We can provide a KMS whitepaper + certification statement as part of the TIA pack.

Operational asks from legal to close:
1) Laura: can you confirm which specific SCCs variant (2010 vs 2021 vs Commission Implementing Act text) Eurythmics expects in the annex? Laura, if you can sync with Sarah on that, we can map the correct template.
2) Neha: agree the timeline — Laura's Tue deadline works for a draft evidence manifest.

I also flagged a routing exception in the Order Form (we are still referencing azure-west-eu as 'primary' without a fallback list). Suggest we add a short clause listing fallback regions; that reduces friction on their side for SLA approvals.

Ben Carter
Sr. Manager, Trust Engineering
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@eurythmicshealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@eurythmicshealth.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCCs mapping questions

Neha / Ben / Laura —

Appreciate the quick review and proposed compromise on notice periods. A few confirmations from our side:

- Eurythmics will accept SCCs as an annex provided the annex explicitly states the Commission Implementing Act (2021) variant.
- We can accept the 14-day prior notice + 30-day review escalation language for non-EU subprocessors, subject to the clause including an ability to pause onboarding for high-risk processors. Please add a short pause-and-escalate sentence.
- TIA evidence: KMS whitepaper + inventory list will be sufficient for initial review. We'll reserve the right to request additional evidence for specific high-risk subs.

I've attached an updated redline (Eurythmics_DPA_redline_v2.docx) which:
- switches the SCCs reference to the 2021 text;
- adds a short pause clause for onboarding outside the EU;
- leaves Order Form routing fallback comment in place;

Can we lock a 30-min call Wed 23 Apr 09:30 PT to finalize the annex text? If we get a clean draft after that call, Procurement will prepare a DocuSign package and aim to circulate by 28 Apr.

Thanks —

Sarah Whitman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Eurythmics Health

Attachments: Eurythmics_DPA_redline_v2.docx
